$comment: The recorded ambiguity count across the golden vectors, as a RATCHET.
An ambiguity is a convention in docs/CONVENTIONS.md that admits two readings. The
two independently authored passes still AGREE on every vector; what this counts is
the number of places where they agreed without the convention having compelled them
to. `rederive:vectors` fails when the count RISES above this number.
One of the recorded ambiguities is substantive rather than presentational:
[denominator] Whether the Art. 10(1) five-percent trigger tests the signed gap or
its magnitude. v08-negative-gap is the only vector in the set where the two
readings give different OUTCOMES rather than different numbers.
That decides whether an employer owes a joint pay assessment, so this file is not
bookkeeping. Raising `count` is accepting a new ambiguity: say who accepted it and
why in `accepted`, in the same diff. Settling one LOWERS the count, and the script
asks for the baseline to be lowered in the same commit so the ratchet cannot slip.
accepted: Baseline recorded while fixing WR-13. These 45 are the ambiguities the phase-01 vectors surfaced; none is newly introduced here. The [denominator] Art. 10(1) signed-gap-versus-magnitude reading is the one that changes an outcome. It is now DECIDED, not carried forward: the MAGNITUDE reading governs, as recorded in docs/CONVENTIONS.md (denominator). Art. 10(1) is engaged by a difference in average pay level of at least 5 % whichever sex it favours, and Art10Flag.gapPct carries the SIGNED value so the direction is never lost. Accepted by the maintainer (marek.rybka1) on 2026-09-14 during phase-01 UAT, on the ground that the signed reading would silently exempt every category in which men are the underpaid group. The remaining 44 ambiguities change numbers, not outcomes.
